chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjāl, from Thaʿlabah, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said:

The qarāʾ (monthly periods) are the aṭhār (clean periods). The other interpretation in the two reports is that the expression was used to refer to three qarāʾ, in that they do not become clear (i.e., the woman is considered pure) except upon seeing the blood of the third period. Thus, he expressed the first sighting of blood as another period by way of metaphor, even if it is not a condition of that to complete the third period, as we have previously stated. And in the report it is not established that she is required to complete the third period, nor does this interpretation contradict it.
ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence define the number of periods required for a woman to be considered pure after menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the definition of *al-qarāʾ* (clean periods) in the context of determining a woman's purity, offering two scholarly interpretations: either referring to the clean intervals themselves or metaphorically linking the first blood sighting to the completion of the third cycle. It highlights the nuanced Shia juristic approach to reconciling textual ambiguity with practical ritual purity laws, emphasizing that the metaphor does not strictly require the full completion of the third period for the ruling to apply.
